newsitem.title: UK: Phillips starts delayed UK J-block oilfield projec.
newsitem.headline: Phillips starts delayed UK J-block oilfield projec.

text.p: U.S. Phillips Petroleum said on Monday it had started oil production from its long-delayed British North Sea Judy and Joanne project at 25,000 barrels a day (bpd).
"Current production is 25,000 barrels a day and should average 35-40,000 barrels a day for the remainder of the year," Phillips UK said in a statement.
Oil from the so-called J-block fields is being exported via the mainly Norwegian Ekofisk stream at Teeside in northeast England.
Output from J-block was delayed by a legal wrangle with U.S. Enron Corp over delivery of gas from the fields.

Original J-block facilities were completed and ready for full production in February 1996 but Enron indicated it would not take gas under its sales agreements with Phillips until at least September 1999.
Phillips elected to reinject gas for later production and delivery but is unable to run oil output at the 95,000 bpd capacity of the Judy platform.
It said the 50 million pound reinjection project was expected to increase recovery rates from J-block by about five percent.
The company is considering developing satellite fields having recently discovered the Jade field north of Judy and appraised the Jacqui field to the east.
Other interests in J-block are held by Agip SpA and BG plc.
